The wrong people fill the void when Democrats stop showing up.
#
Peter,
When Democrats stop showing up, the wrong people fill the void.
We’ve seen it happen in too many places. Entire communities get written off. Schools get underfunded. Hospitals close. Good jobs disappear. And then Republicans show up with scapegoats, culture-war bullcrap, and billionaire-backed candidates who have no real plan to make life better.
That is how they keep people angry at each other while nothing gets fixed. _So we have to show up earlier, organize harder, and compete in more places._
We’re not waiting until the final weeks of an election to parachute in with a TV ad and hope for the best. We’re organizing earlier, recruiting stronger candidates, and helping Democrats compete in places too many people gave up on.
That means supporting leaders who know their communities — people who will fight for schools, jobs, health care, child care, and the basic building blocks that make a place strong.
**Because if we don’t fill that void with real organizing, someone else will fill it with noise.**

body:

Derek,
I’m the hope and change guy, but I’ll be honest: we’ve got some real work to do in this country. And if we want to make progress, we’ll need leaders who tell the truth, tackle hard problems, and serve the people who put them in office in the first place.
The good news is we have the chance to elect leaders like that _this year_ — in both houses of Congress, governorships, state legislatures, and offices up and down the ballot.
But it’s going to take all of us to do it.
**It’s up to all of us, as citizens, to stand up for our values. We can’t just leave it to somebody else. We have to fight, even when it’s hard.**
Republicans want you to think that a few people in power make all the decisions and the rest of us have to live with the consequences. But when you look at the history of America, real change has always come from the bottom up — from ordinary folks who make it happen.
So yes, we are being tested. But we have the power, as citizens, to change this country.
We’ve just got to use it.
Derek, the DNC is the only organization working to elect the Democratic leaders we need at all levels of government, all across the country. When you chip in to the DNC, you’re supporting thousands of candidates we must elect this year.
[**So, today, I am asking you to contribute whatever you can to the DNC. name: Texas Organizing Project
subject: Have you voted? 🗳️
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
JUNE 11: Data Center Documentary & Discussion
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Data%20Center%20event.png]
Across Texas and our country, tech giants are building data centers and our communities are paying the price. These facilities threaten us with higher water bills, increased pollution, public health risks, and added strain on our already unstable energy grid. We need to put our communities before this corporate slop.
JOIN TOP for a FREE documentary screening and discussion [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2] with community members to learn how data centers impact our everyday lives.
📆 Thursday, June 11th at 6 p.m.
📍 Texas Theatre in Dallas (231 Jefferson Blvd)
🏆 Attendees have a chance to win a $100 gift card!
For more information, contact Jet at (469) 550-4750.
https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2]
EARLY VOTING: Polls are now open
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20PAC%20canvass%20with%20Adrian%20Reyna.jpg]
Early voting in the Texas Democratic Primary Runoff election is happening NOW and it runs through this Friday, May 22. Election Day is Tuesday, May 26. That's not a lot of time, so make a plan to head to the polls!
Make sure to support people-powered progressive candidates who will move our state and communities forward. Check who will be on your ballot [https://www.ballotready.org/us/texas] , and vote for TOP-endorsed candidates this runoff.
✅ Christian Menefee for Congress, TX-18
✅ Marcos Vélez for TX Lt. Governor
✅ Adrian Reyna for TX House, Dist. 125
✅ Dexter McCoy for Fort Bend County Judge
✅ Letitia Plummer for Harris County Judge
TOP IN ACTION: Moderating a conversation with Democracy Now!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Tiffany%20at%20Amy%20Goodman%20screening.png]
TOP Policy & Development Director Tiffany Hogue had the honor and pleasure of moderating a discussion featuring legendary journalist Amy Goodman of Democracy Now! this past Saturday at the River Oaks Theatre in Houston.
The discussion followed a showing of "Steal This Story, Please!" [https://stealthisstory.org/] — a documentary spotlighting the life and career of Goodman, a tireless independent investigative journalist who for decades has been a staple at Democracy Now! The documentary couldn't be more timely, as Trump's regime continues to clamp down on freedom of the press and the First Amendment as a whole.
Learn more about it, and get your tickets. [https://stealthisstory.org/]
May 30: Dallas Right2Justice Member Retreat
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dallas%20R2J%20members.jpg]
TOP's Right2Justice (R2J) campaign is continuing to sharpen around probation reform, non-safety traffic stops, and the broader criminalization pipeline — including the criminalizing of immigrant communities across the country.
Attend our next R2J member retreat on Saturday, May 30 in Dallas to learn more on latest campaign developments and how we can expand our efforts.
Contact Dr. Doshie Piper at dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] for more retreat details and to reserve your spot.
TOP Tip: Look out for yourself and others this Mental Health Awareness Month
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Mental%20health%20awareness%20month.png]
May is Mental Health Awareness Month, an annual campaign dedicated to raising awareness about mental illness, reducing stigma, and promoting mental well-being . Nearly 1 in 5 American adults will have a diagnosable mental health condition in any given year, showing that no matter your age, race, or background, mental health impacts each and every one of us over the course of our lives. Read up on quick facts and stats about mental health, as well as how you can access basic mental health resources. [https://mhanational.org/resources/quick-facts-and-statistics-about-mental-health/]
Español
11 de junio: Documental sobre centros de datos y debate
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Data%20Center%20event.png]
En todo Texas y en nuestro país, los gigantes tecnológicos están construyendo centros de datos, y nuestras comunidades están pagando el precio. Estas instalaciones nos amenazan con costos de agua más elevados, mayor contaminación, riesgos para la salud pública y una presión adicional sobre nuestra ya inestable red energética. Debemos poner a nuestras comunidades antes que a esta voracidad corporativa.
Únete a TOP para asistir a la proyección GRATUITA de un documental y participar en un debate [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2] con miembros de la comunidad para conocer cómo los centros de datos impactan nuestra vida cotidiana.
📆 Jueves, 11 de junio a las 6:00 p.m.
📍 Texas Theatre en Dallas (231 Jefferson Blvd)
🏆 ¡Los asistentes tendrán la oportunidad de ganar una tarjeta de regalo de $100!
Para más información, comunícate con Jet al (469) 550-4750.
https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/brQtPZN3UUCF83a4PjDSHw2]
VOTACIÓN TEMPRANA: Los centros de votación ya están abiertos
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/TOP%20PAC%20canvass%20with%20Adrian%20Reyna.jpg]
La votación temprana para la segunda vuelta de las primarias demócratas de Texas se está llevando a cabo AHORA mismo y continuará hasta este viernes, 22 de mayo. El día de las elecciones es el martes, 26 de mayo. ¡No queda mucho tiempo, así que haga un plan para acudir a las urnas!
Asegúrese de apoyar a los candidatos progresistas impulsados por la gente, quienes harán avanzar a nuestro estado y a nuestras comunidades. Verifique quiénes aparecerán en su boleta electoral [https://www.ballotready.org/us/texas] y vote por los candidatos respaldados por TOP en esta segunda vuelta.
✅ Christian Menefee para el Congreso, TX-18
✅ Marcos Vélez para Vicegobernador de TX
✅ Adrian Reyna para la Cámara de Representantes de TX, Dist. 125
✅ Dexter McCoy para Juez del Condado de Fort Bend
✅ Letitia Plummer para Jueza del Condado de Harris
TOP EN ACCIÓN: Moderando una conversación con Democracy Now!
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Tiffany%20at%20Amy%20Goodman%20screening.png]
Tiffany Hogue, Directora de Política y Desarrollo de TOP, tuvo el honor y el placer de moderar una conversación con la legendaria periodista Amy Goodman, de *Democracy Now!*, el pasado sábado en el River Oaks Theatre de Houston.
La conversación tuvo lugar tras la proyección de *Steal This Story, Please!* [https://stealthisstory.org/] , un documental que destaca la vida y la trayectoria de Goodman, una incansable periodista de investigación independiente que, durante décadas, ha sido una figura fundamental en *Democracy Now!*.
El documental no podría ser más oportuno, dado que el régimen de Trump continúa reprimiendo la libertad de prensa y la Primera Enmienda en su conjunto.
Obtenga más información y adquiera sus entradas. [https://stealthisstory.org/]
30 de mayo: Retiro de miembros de Dallas Right2Justice
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Dallas%20R2J%20members.jpg]
La campaña Right2Justice (R2J) de TOP continúa enfocándose cada vez más en la reforma del régimen de libertad condicional, las detenciones de tráfico no relacionadas con la seguridad y el proceso más amplio de criminalización —incluida la criminalización de las comunidades inmigrantes en todo el país.
Asista a nuestro próximo retiro de miembros de R2J el sábado 30 de mayo en Dallas para conocer los últimos avances de la campaña y descubrir cómo podemos ampliar nuestros esfuerzos.
Comuníquese con la Dra. Doshie Piper en dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] para obtener más detalles sobre el retiro y reservar su lugar.
Consejos de TOP: Cuida de ti mismo y de los demás durante este Mes de Concienciación sobre la Salud Mental
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Mental%20health%20awareness%20month.png]
Mayo es el Mes de la Concientización sobre la Salud Mental, una campaña anual dedicada a crear conciencia sobre las enfermedades mentales, reducir el estigma y promover el bienestar mental. Casi 1 de cada 5 adultos estadounidenses presentará una afección de salud mental diagnosticable en un año determinado, lo que demuestra que, independientemente de su edad, raza u origen, la salud mental nos afecta a todos y cada uno de nosotros a lo largo de nuestra vida. Infórmese sobre datos breves y estadísticas acerca de la salud mental, así como sobre la manera de acceder a recursos básicos de salud mental. [https://mhanational.org/resources/quick-facts-and-statistics-about-mental-health/]

I wanted you to hear this from me first:
**I 'm suing Donald Trump.**
As a Capitol Police Officer, I held the line on January 6th to defend democracy and the rule of law. Now, Trump is starting a slush fund to REWARD the rioters who beat me and my fellow officers bloody. _And YOUR taxpayer dollars are funding it._
I'm PISSED. This $1.8 BILLION slush fund is Trump's way of BANKROLLING people who incite violence on his behalf.
On January 6, I was immersed in a profane mix of sweat, screams, blood, broken limbs, hatred, and bigotry as Trump's mob tried to overturn a free and fair election. When I testified about the horrors of that day, I faced a barrage of death threats. Donald Trump just put another target on my back.
But I refuse to back down. I will stand up to Donald Trump today and I will stand up to him in Washington as MD-05's next Congressman.
#### **[First, I need your help to get there. This moment calls for Democrats who are ready to hold Trump accountable at every turn. Can you help me overcome the whopping $1.5 million of dark money in my primary so I can win this race to fight back against Donald Trump?>>](https://substack.com/redirect/dafe3059-bf89-4783-a15e-e5cb315bfd5d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thanks for standing with me.
-- Harry Dunn

These victories matter. Because in some of the toughest races of 2026, voters made clear what we already know: Democratic pro-choice women are ready to take on Republicans, fight for our rights, and win in November.

But last night was just the beginning.

Now, our candidates need to build the kind of formidable general election campaigns it will take to sustain this momentum through November — because now that they are the official Democratic nominees, they’re about to become top targets for Republican attacks, outside spending, and every attempt to slow them down.

These victories matter. Because in some of the toughest races of 2026, voters made clear what we already know: Democratic pro-choice women are ready to take on Republicans, fight for our rights, and win in November. But last night was just the beginning. subject: It’s my constituents who are deployed in this war

It’s been 81 days since Donald Trump started his stupid, reckless war in Iran.
Thousands of San Diego-based sailors and Marines have already deployed to the region, and thousands more have received 48-hour deployment notices.
These are our neighbors, our friends, people we see at grocery stores and on the sidewalk.
I’m keenly aware of the fact that when our president decides to take military action against another country, legally or illegally, it’s my constituents — the San Diego-based service members — who are sent into harm’s way.
They sacrifice their bodies, their mental health, their time with loved ones, and even their lives for us. While they’re willing to make those sacrifices, we in Congress need to be damn sure it’s worth it. And I can say without a shadow of a doubt that this war of choice in Iran is not worth that risk or sacrifice.
That’s why I introduced a War Powers Resolution in the House to end Donald Trump's war in Iran and bring my constituents home. And it’s why I’m voting YES on Ranking Member Meeks’ War Powers Resolution on the House floor later today.
Our service members deserve better than to be treated as expendable pawns in Trump’s political games — and so do the American people, who are being forced to pay over $1 billion per day for this military adventurism.
My resolution will get a vote on the floor in the coming weeks, and we will keep pushing War Powers Resolutions until they pass. So I’m coming to you for your help.
Will you add your name and let me know that you support my War Powers Resolution to bring our troops home? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/p3cwElIz5UOKNmdoscYyMg2]
ADD MY NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/p3cwElIz5UOKNmdoscYyMg2]
Our service members are counting on us.
–Sara

They sacrifice their bodies, their mental health, their time with loved ones, and even their lives for us. While they’re willing to make those sacrifices, we in Congress need to be damn sure it’s worth it. And I can say without a shadow of a doubt that this war of choice in Iran is not worth that risk or sacrifice. That’s why I introduced a War Powers Resolution in the House to end Donald Trump's war in Iran and bring my constituents home. And it’s why I’m voting YES on Ranking Member Meeks’ War Powers Resolution on the House floor later today. Our service members deserve better than to be treated as expendable pawns in Trump’s political games — and so do the American people, who are being forced to pay over $1 billion per day for this military adventurism. My resolution will get a vote on the floor in the coming weeks, and we will keep pushing War Powers Resolutions until they pass. So I’m coming to you for your help. Will you add your name and let me know that you support my War Powers Resolution to bring our troops home? subject: This is what delegalization looks like
body:
Delegalization is happening across the country as officials dismantle the legal protections many immigrants have had for decades. | | |
Peter, In deeply alarming news, The New York Times reported that the Justice Department has identified 384 naturalized U.S. citizens from whom they want to strip citizenship. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIdicNPDEjB8U81Sf47SIVH6uNxujjX6zH2gVOwoU3uUKDGx32N_mOLS8i9D1ya2vlaRd2LdMsBNFA6kqc4-TxENSFIGvyj5Y3qhlPBnLwsGzene6KBE9cn9LC-pbrbHNLbvOPqW5-Ub42a8krRZ44LJUO2EQBFQxszFgCSms0SeR5XL3jzLbZic6MAx_40kmohbVZuJD9CVM2L-vt0HHxrX_hXAvoqaJ2pMl8g5moYCuoj4iTcJUSrIMzltvt6XzRGxsSsLv5R78iLOoLg5cfvNoFD5qT2n17-0Hj6G9Mpyf0hqqnEC6MRCATUSmJyNMgTUnR2SGC1SPsB_nJiQUB2f8riv1wqe1Cd2nGDxGQosEC7-7H1DluJXB6edqQE8Q/4qs/X56iXeNLS6KqoHVt3R0vEg/h0/h001.XMsvszPVOQoOBSdbsWENbtL9s3QO2aS27oZ_AOlqkiU) This attack is part of a much larger pattern of efforts meant to revoke status from our communities and delegalize people en masse. One by one, officials are dismantling the legal protections many immigrants have relied on and had for decades. For DACA recipients, this is already real: USCIS delays in processing DACA renewals are leading to lapses in status and thousands of DACA recipients being left exposed to detention and deportation. A recent decision from the Justice Department also makes it easier to deport DACA recipients, eroding the very protections the program was intended to uphold. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeIdicNPDEjB8U81Sf47SIVH6uNxujjX6zH2gVOwoU3uUKDGx32N_mOLS8i9D1ya2vlaRd2LdMsBNFA6kqc4-TxM62aQnzZKU0PW6BGKKbLeTV8dHjmvC1naTcuNpJurMnrso-Jdb_zBS86_QOUBYvayeoxVAwG49rXX8KxJfN7bJQOvih0NKVZDN0izsjbY8eQGamDXbsbOxXOUgUguCDvNavo3-yDsMtIi_zus5ybX93pzkjJ6CG-lWhTuZzxxIxmy1DwYcilUpZlK0HHFcecKq6Yl0BB3M_M_3YjjTfnrdF5es1IYcp7lpWc6Qn2JL5jnRntkT24Tv1abkdO9gye2VynWR5G49OAF2IHYFhbsY4lNyDAuilolv117ffK1Cx/4qs/X56iXeNLS6KqoHVt3R0vEg/h1/h001.cr71Nj6o78BITlkjCIGOWeXgSwlgXuQf6Y4ZyhImdKA) At the same time, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) programs are also being weakened, asylum processes are being blocked and delayed, and refugee resettlement is being slashed. **Peter, it’s clear that mass delegalization is unfolding in real time through a steady, coordinated effort to erase status, dismantle critical programs like DACA and TPS, and put millions of families at risk.** _We need your help to fight back and protect our communities now._ **[The fight to protect DACA recipients is urgent. Our organizing must be as well. United We Dream relies on your help to fuel our advocacy efforts. clean_body: Delegalization is happening across the country as officials dismantle the legal protections many immigrants have had for decades. | | | Peter, In deeply alarming news, The New York Times reported that the Justice Department has identified 384 naturalized U.S. citizens from whom they want to strip citizenship. This attack is part of a much larger pattern of efforts meant to revoke status from our communities and delegalize people en masse. One by one, officials are dismantling the legal protections many immigrants have relied on and had for decades. For DACA recipients, this is already real: USCIS delays in processing DACA renewals are leading to lapses in status and thousands of DACA recipients being left exposed to detention and deportation. A recent decision from the Justice Department also makes it easier to deport DACA recipients, eroding the very protections the program was intended to uphold. At the same time, Temporary Protected Status (TPS) programs are also being weakened, asylum processes are being blocked and delayed, and refugee resettlement is being slashed. Peter, it’s clear that mass delegalization is unfolding in real time through a steady, coordinated effort to erase status, dismantle critical programs like DACA and TPS, and put millions of families at risk. We need your help to fight back and protect our communities now. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | In this moment of deeply alarming attacks on our immigrant neighbors and loved ones, you have shown up for our communities, Peter. name: Cleo Fields
subject: If I have to be white to serve, I can't change that. But I can fight.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CLEO FIELDS FOR CONGRESS
body:
I represented Louisiana in Congress from 1993 to 1996. Then they gerrymandered me out. In 2024, a federal court reinstated my district. I ran and I won after 28 years away. But the new district didn’t
| | | | | [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019YuLtwwHCFo_eMuVyy-XxRSsU9bjeWucQDUEkMZBOM7AM-btzu2_JFen0fv5dtYyvih0Pp7pFGvpHVtv_TjwJy5memC-VTqe96lhRwnKJ02nBhQvDti3moFrq_-T2Tk02iE0m89TeeXTnz4x-voYo3wJ1Q47ISrGDzV5m4HciV4GE1uXI9yD7S4MFc9fA896lbaK51B7TRO_txxAGoiLhw==&c=yElLzBC2cHVQuOIzuQnp9HHGbE0JpQ9Hy0We_ELHcAeJJpI0ZV-Rgw==&ch=QRKAtBFaqAMHwAQl05bcZWjshaOnWVyOns-0vAVOR9uu6e8EdDrdcg==)
---
| Peter,
I was 24 years old when I walked into the Louisiana State Senate. No money or establishment machine behind me. Just a kid from Baton Rouge who wrote his own radio jingles and knocked on every door himself. People said I couldn't win. I won anyway.
Five years later, I took that same drive, that same refusal to be counted out, all the way to the United States Congress.
While I was there, I built the Congressional Classroom, a first-of-its-kind program that brought elementary and high school students to DC to see themselves as future leaders. I fought for job creation, affordable health care, and economic opportunity for the people back home. I gave everything I had to that job.
Then they gerrymandered me out. Redrew the lines, erased my district, and sent me home. That was 1996. I was 33 years old.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019YuLtwwHCFo_eMuVyy-XxRSsU9bjeWucQDUEkMZBOM7AM-btzu2_JFen0fv5dtYyvih0Pp7pFGvpHVtv_TjwJy5memC-VTqe96lhRwnKJ02nBhQvDti3moFrq_-T2Tk02iE0m89TeeXTnz4x-voYo3wJ1Q47ISrGDzV5m4HciV4GE1uXI9yD7S4MFc9fA896lbaK51B7TRNp975vruhWcA==&c=yElLzBC2cHVQuOIzuQnp9HHGbE0JpQ9Hy0We_ELHcAeJJpI0ZV-Rgw==&ch=QRKAtBFaqAMHwAQl05bcZWjshaOnWVyOns-0vAVOR9uu6e8EdDrdcg==)
---
Me in 1995. Standing on the steps of the Supreme Court, fighting to keep my seat.
I spent the next 28 years serving Louisiana another way -- in the State Senate, in the courtroom, building the Louisiana Leadership Institute into something that has transformed thousands of young people's lives.
I never stopped fighting. I never stopped believing that all Louisianans deserved a voice in Congress that represented their interests.
In 2024, a federal court agreed. Louisiana is one-third Black. It has six congressional seats. For decades, only one of them gave Black voters a real opportunity to elect a representative of their choice. The court ordered that it be fixed.
I ran for the new majority-Black district. I won after 28 years away. And the district didn't even survive for my full term.
---
| [](https://eub669hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019YuLtwwHCFo_eMuVyy-XxRSsU9bjeWucQDUEkMZBOM7AM-btzu2_JFen0fv5dtYyvih0Pp7pFGvpHVtv_TjwJy5memC-VTqe96lhRwnKJ02nBhQvDti3moFrq_-T2Tk02iE0m89TeeXTnz4x-voYo3wJ1Q47ISrGDzV5m4HciV4GE1uXI9yD7S4MFc9fA896lbaK51B7TRMiEX1q3VDGAA==&c=yElLzBC2cHVQuOIzuQnp9HHGbE0JpQ9Hy0We_ELHcAeJJpI0ZV-Rgw==&ch=QRKAtBFaqAMHwAQl05bcZWjshaOnWVyOns-0vAVOR9uu6e8EdDrdcg==)
---
Thirty years later, I'm back in the Louisiana State Capitol fighting the exact same fight.
Three weeks ago, the Supreme Court struck down my district when they gutted the Voting Rights Act. And MAGA Governor Jeff Landry didn't hesitate. He canceled an active election, throwing out over 45,000 absentee ballots already cast by real Louisiana voters, to fast-track a new gerrymander designed to draw me out of existence.
The same dirty trick decades later. The message to Black people is unchanged: your seat at the table is not permanent. We can take it back whenever we want.
My response? If they tell me I have to be white to serve in Congress from Louisiana, I cannot change that. But I refuse to go quietly. I have fought for this state my entire life. I am not done yet. And I am asking you to stand with me:
[This will be an uphill battle. But I have never backed down from a fight I believed in. The Democratic proponents of redistricting felt a devastating blow on Friday when the Supreme Court of Virginia handed down a 4-3 decision overturning the results of the special referendum election, stating that the procedure used by the Virginia General Assembly to pass this Constitutional Amendment was, ironically, unconstitutional. Their reasoning was that Democratic Leadership's definition of an "intervening election" did not fit SCOVA's definition, as "voting had already commenced" for the 2025 election by the time the special session was called.
And of course, the response was predictable. Ridicule and gloating from the Right were all over X, despite them not conceding the fact that they did in fact lose an election, but it was only when the referees intervened and handed them the game that they were "triumphant." Kind of an asterisk if you asked me.
Then came all of the "what you guys should be doing" from Democrats and allies from all over the country. A lot of people were pressuring Governor Spanberger to just "do it anyway" because "that's what the Republicans would do." Many were chastising Virginia Democrats for giving up so easily when the decision came in, even after Virginia Democrats had spent the better part of their holiday season and the beginning of 2026, when most people were either resting or preparing for the midterms, focusing on this snap election.
The one proposal that caught fire was from Quinn Yeargain in the[ Downballot](https://substack.com/redirect/805206f5-d29b-4765-b213-f66e584e3b34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) newsletter and it spread quickly. Yeargain proposed that the Democrats in Virginia should lower the retirement age of Supreme Court Justices in Virginia to 54 which would then force all 7 of the current sitting justices to retire and the Democratic General Assembly could appoint 7 new justices who would vote in the proposed maps anyway.
This proposal was so appealing to Democratic Speaker of the House hopeful Hakeem Jeffries that he called members of the Virginia Congressional Delegation to tell them it should be the plan moving forward. Jeffries was so adamant that Democrats should do whatever they could to get this across the finish line and protect our democracy that this was a necessary action on their part.
You know who all of these people forgot to ask? Virginia State Democrats.
Governor Spanberger, who would need to sign off on this lowering of the age, was not briefed or consulted beforehand. Speaker of the House Don Scott was not consulted by Jeffries or anyone else pushing this narrative in the open, and he would have to lead the effort to appoint replacements for these justices.
Senate Majority Leader Scott Surovell even said it was not possible, calling the idea "too extreme" and explaining it "would not have time under the current system used at the Department of Elections, to make the changes." He said he wants to work within the current legal system to do these kinds of things.
But the biggest takeaway was this: Virginia Democrats answered the call to action when they saw what was happening in Texas and Missouri and what was bound to happen in other states. They took the risk to push back when the rest of the country was watching to see if anyone would. They knocked doors in February. They cut ads. They sat through committee hearings on a constitutional amendment most voters had never heard of three months earlier. They lost a 4-3 decision that turned on a procedural definition of "intervening election" that most of the people now demanding action have never read.
And then on Monday morning, the calls started coming in from people who had not made a single one of those phone calls themselves.
* * *
## **The states that didn 't show up are loud now.**
Here is the part nobody wants to say out loud: Virginia and California were alone.
California has a Democratic trifecta. Newsom called a special election to redraw maps and the voters approved it. They proved they could do it. Maryland has already started the process in their Democratic trifecta.
New York has a Democratic trifecta. Illinois has a Democratic trifecta. Massachusetts. Washington. Oregon. Colorado. New Jersey. Delaware. Connecticut. New Mexico. Minnesota. Every one of these states had the legal architecture and the political majorities to respond to what Texas and Missouri did. Most of them did nothing. A few made noise about studying it. None of them put a constitutional amendment on the ballot in the middle of an election year and asked their voters to expand the legislature's redistricting power.
Virginia did.
Virginia lost on a 4-3 procedural ruling that turned on whether early voting for the November 2025 general election had "commenced" by the time the General Assembly called the special session. That is the entire ballgame. Not the substance of the maps. Not the fairness of the process. Not the will of the voters who approved the amendment in April. A definitional question about the word "commenced."
And now Hakeem Jeffries, who represents Brooklyn, wants to call the Virginia Delegation and ignore the state level Democrats who actually have insight and authority over this process.
Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, to his credit, said publicly that Democrats need a strong stomach right now. He is right about that. He is also a member of Congress, not a member of the Virginia General Assembly, and the people who would actually have to pass the bill, sign the bill, defend the bill in court, and appoint the replacement justices were not the ones on those Monday morning calls.
The Virginia officials who would have to execute this plan said no. Not because they are timid. Not because they lack a strong stomach. Because they spent the last six months actually doing the work and they understand, in a way that someone calling from a New York office does not, what it costs to do this twice.
* * *
## **" That's what Republicans would do" is not a strategy.**
The loudest argument for the Yeargain proposal was that Republicans would do it. That is true. Republicans absolutely would lower a retirement age to clear a court they did not like. Republicans absolutely would ignore precedent, fire the referee, and walk off with the trophy.
That is not a recommendation. That is a description of the problem.
The argument that Democrats should match Republicans procedural-norm-violation-for-procedural-norm-violation assumes that the only thing keeping the system upright is which team is willing to pull the load-bearing wall down first. It is the political equivalent of a hostage situation where the proposed solution is for the hostages to take their own captives.
And it is being made, almost exclusively, by people who do not have to face the voters who would have to live with the precedent.
Don Scott has to face Portsmouth in 2027. Surovell has to hold a Senate majority that runs through Loudoun, Prince William, and Henrico, where the suburban voters who delivered the April amendment by three points are the same voters who will decide whether "Democrats will not destroy the courts to win" is a credible message in 2026 and 2027. Spanberger does not run again -- Virginia is the only state in the country that limits its governor to a single term -- but every Democrat who wants her seat in 2029 does, and the precedent she signs becomes the precedent they have to defend.
Jeffries, if he becomes Speaker, will face a national midterm where the median voter has never heard the words "Stephen McCullough" and never will.
These are different jobs. They require different calculations. The Virginians making the calculation are the ones whose names go on the ballot.
* * *
## **What the people calling forgot.**
The Yeargain proposal, on its analytical merits, is a serious piece of work. Quinn Yeargain is one of the sharpest election-law writers in the country and The Downballot is one of the few publications still doing real structural reporting on state-level democracy. The proposal identifies a real legal mechanism. It identifies the right justice (McCullough, the youngest in the 4-3 majority, currently 54). It walks through the implementation. Read it. They did the work.
The proposal is not the problem.
The problem is the gap between a newsletter post on Friday and a national Speaker-hopeful putting it on a phone call on Monday morning, without making one of those phone calls to the people who would have to do it.
There is a name for this in every functional political operation in the country: it is called freelancing. And the reason functional operations do not tolerate it is that the consequences of a freelanced strategy do not land on the freelancer. They land on the governor who has to veto, the speaker who has to whip, and the senate leader who has to explain to his caucus why they spent a week defending a proposal they were never asked about.
Virginia spent six months building a coalition to expand fair maps. That coalition included CleanVA, the unions, every constitutional officer who put their name on the line, and 51% of the voters who showed up in April to approve the amendment in the middle of an off-year cycle most pundits had already written off.
The Supreme Court of Virginia overturned that work on a definition of "commenced."
The right response is not to overturn the court. The right response is to make sure the next coalition is bigger, the next amendment is procedurally airtight, and the next time someone in another state is asked to match Virginia's effort, they actually do it.
* * *
## **Where the good guys are.**
The title of this piece is a question because it is the question I keep getting asked. Where are the good guys? Where is the cavalry? Why is it always Virginia, always Lucas, always Scott, always Spanberger, always the same handful of people doing the work while everyone else watches and grades it on a curve afterward?
The good guys are in Richmond. They are in Norfolk and Charlottesville and Arlington and Roanoke. They are the volunteers who knocked doors in February for a constitutional amendment most of them could not explain in one sentence. They are the General Assembly Democrats who took the vote knowing it could fail and took it anyway.
The good guys are also the ones who, on Monday morning, said no to a plan that would have made every future Republican attack on Democratic norm-violation easier to land. They said no because they have to live in the state after the cameras leave.
Show up before you give advice. Knock the doors. Cut the checks. Call your own governor before you call somebody else's. And when a state with a Democratic trifecta loses a 4-3 ruling on a definition of "commenced," do not show up on day three with a proposal that requires that same state to do the next round of work alone.
Virginia did the work. The rest of the country owes Virginia something more than a phone call about what to do next.
They'll remember who showed up. They'll remember who didn't.

## **TL;DR**
* The Supreme Court of Virginia overturned the redistricting amendment 4-3 on a procedural definition of "intervening election," not on the substance of the maps.
* Quinn Yeargain in The Downballot proposed lowering the mandatory judicial retirement age to 54 to force the majority off the court. Hakeem Jeffries adopted the proposal on Monday morning calls to Virginia members of Congress.
* Spanberger was not briefed. Don Scott was not consulted. Surovell called the idea "too extreme" and said the Department of Elections cannot execute it in time anyway.
* Subramanyam supported the plan. He is the exception, not the consensus, and he is not the one who would have to execute it.
* Virginia is the only Democratic-trifecta state that actually built and ran a redistricting response in 2026. California ran their own and won. Every other Democratic trifecta did nothing.
* The argument "Republicans would do it" describes the problem, not the solution. Spanberger cannot run again -- Virginia is the only state with a one-term limit on its governor -- but Don Scott faces Portsmouth in 2027, Surovell has to hold a Senate majority through the same suburbs that delivered the April amendment, and the next Democrat to want the Governor's Mansion will inherit whatever precedent gets signed this winter.
* Show up before you give advice. Virginia did the work. The next time someone needs help, the people who spent April knocking doors for a constitutional amendment they did not write should not have to do it alone.

Spanberger does not run again -- Virginia is the only state in the country that limits its governor to a single term -- but every Democrat who wants her seat in 2029 does, and the precedent she signs becomes the precedent they have to defend. Jeffries, if he becomes Speaker, will face a national midterm where the median voter has never heard the words "Stephen McCullough" and never will. These are different jobs. They require different calculations. The Virginians making the calculation are the ones whose names go on the ballot. What the people calling forgot. The Yeargain proposal, on its analytical merits, is a serious piece of work. Quinn Yeargain is one of the sharpest election-law writers in the country and The Downballot is one of the few publications still doing real structural reporting on state-level democracy. The proposal identifies a real legal mechanism. It identifies the right justice (McCullough, the youngest in the 4-3 majority, currently 54). It walks through the implementation. Read it. They did the work. The proposal is not the problem. The problem is the gap between a newsletter post on Friday and a national Speaker-hopeful putting it on a phone call on Monday morning, without making one of those phone calls to the people who would have to do it. There is a name for this in every functional political operation in the country: it is called freelancing. And the reason functional operations do not tolerate it is that the consequences of a freelanced strategy do not land on the freelancer. They land on the governor who has to veto, the speaker who has to whip, and the senate leader who has to explain to his caucus why they spent a week defending a proposal they were never asked about. Virginia spent six months building a coalition to expand fair maps. That coalition included CleanVA, the unions, every constitutional officer who put their name on the line, and 51% of the voters who showed up in April to approve the amendment in the middle of an off-year cycle most pundits had already written off. The Supreme Court of Virginia overturned that work on a definition of "commenced." The right response is not to overturn the court. The right response is to make sure the next coalition is bigger, the next amendment is procedurally airtight, and the next time someone in another state is asked to match Virginia's effort, they actually do it. Where the good guys are. The title of this piece is a question because it is the question I keep getting asked. Where are the good guys? Where is the cavalry? Why is it always Virginia, always Lucas, always Scott, always Spanberger, always the same handful of people doing the work while everyone else watches and grades it on a curve afterward? The good guys are in Richmond. They are in Norfolk and Charlottesville and Arlington and Roanoke. They are the volunteers who knocked doors in February for a constitutional amendment most of them could not explain in one sentence. They are the General Assembly Democrats who took the vote knowing it could fail and took it anyway. The good guys are also the ones who, on Monday morning, said no to a plan that would have made every future Republican attack on Democratic norm-violation easier to land. They said no because they have to live in the state after the cameras leave. Show up before you give advice. Knock the doors. Cut the checks. Call your own governor before you call somebody else's. And when a state with a Democratic trifecta loses a 4-3 ruling on a definition of "commenced," do not show up on day three with a proposal that requires that same state to do the next round of work alone. Virginia did the work. The rest of the country owes Virginia something more than a phone call about what to do next. They'll remember who showed up. They'll remember who didn't. Thanks for reading By the Ballot! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. ? TL;DR The Supreme Court of Virginia overturned the redistricting amendment 4-3 on a procedural definition of "intervening election," not on the substance of the maps. Quinn Yeargain in The Downballot proposed lowering the mandatory judicial retirement age to 54 to force the majority off the court. Hakeem Jeffries adopted the proposal on Monday morning calls to Virginia members of Congress. Spanberger was not briefed. Don Scott was not consulted. Surovell called the idea "too extreme" and said the Department of Elections cannot execute it in time anyway. Subramanyam supported the plan. He is the exception, not the consensus, and he is not the one who would have to execute it. Virginia is the only Democratic-trifecta state that actually built and ran a redistricting response in 2026. California ran their own and won. Every other Democratic trifecta did nothing. The argument "Republicans would do it" describes the problem, not the solution. Spanberger cannot run again -- Virginia is the only state with a one-term limit on its governor -- but Don Scott faces Portsmouth in 2027, Surovell has to hold a Senate majority through the same suburbs that delivered the April amendment, and the next Democrat to want the Governor's Mansion will inherit whatever precedent gets signed this winter. Show up before you give advice. Virginia did the work. The next time someone needs help, the people who spent April knocking doors for a constitutional amendment they did not write should not have to do it alone. Thanks for reading By the Ballot! Hey folks,
**Adam Mockler** and I went deep on this one.
We talked about the billionaire class, money in politics, Elon Musk buying influence in plain sight, and why so many Americans feel like the system has stopped working for them entirely. We got personal. We got fired up. This conversation hit a nerve because people are exhausted watching the rich rig the rules while everyone else gets left behind.
This is one of those conversations where you can feel the frustration boiling over -- but also the hope that we can still fix this if enough people decide they're done accepting the status quo.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:03**] We break down Elon Musk's alleged "lottery" scheme during the election and how billionaire money distorts democracy in real time.
* [**00:04:35**] I explain why the Republican establishment is trying to purge Thomas Massie -- and what it says about loyalty, war, and corruption in Washington.

name: Eric Burlison for Congress
subject: The scoreboard is in. Every Democrat map challenge lost.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Eric Burlison for Congress]()
body:
Democrats tried to win in court what they couldn't win at the polls.

| | | | | [|
---](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=cbe4573895&e=5f9dc01b8c)
| | Peter ,

I want to walk you through something the national press is not going to put on the front page, because the story does not flatter the people they cover for.The redistricting fight of the last two years is over. The courts have ruled. The maps are in. And the scoreboard is one-sided in a way that, frankly, even I did not expect.**Here is what actually happened.** Last week, the Virginia Supreme Court struck down the maps that Virginia Democrats had spent the better part of two years trying to ram through. The court did not just say the maps had problems. The court said the entire process Democrats used to draw and pass them was unlawful under the Virginia Constitution.That was not the only Democrat loss. The U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Louisiana's racial gerrymander — a map the activist groups had been celebrating for months as the model for the rest of the country. SCOTUS struck it down.Meanwhile — Missouri's new map: upheld. Texas: upheld. Tennessee just signed its new map into law. Alabama and South Carolina are considering similar moves.**Every single Democrat legal challenge to a lawful, Republican-drawn map has failed.** Every. Single. One.And the reason is not complicated.Republican states followed their own constitutions. We drew our maps inside the lines the law actually allows. We put them through the processes our state constitutions actually require. We did the work.Democrats did not. The Virginia Democrats spent tens of millions of dollars on a scheme that included putting outright lies on the ballot to mislead the voters they needed to pass it. They got caught. The court told them so. They got exactly what they deserved.**Now here is why I am writing to you about this today.** The temptation, when you read a scoreboard like that, is to lean back and feel like the fight is over. It is not. The fight just resets.The same activist groups that just lost in Virginia, Louisiana, Missouri, and Texas are not going home. They are already moving money into the 2026 cycle, and they are already drawing target lists. And the seats they target are not the safe ones in deep-blue cities. The seats they target are the conservative seats they want to flip.Missouri's 7th — my seat — is on that list. It has been on that list since I was first elected, and it stays on that list every cycle. The lawful Republican map that just got upheld is exactly what makes this district worth fighting for, both for me and for the people who want to take it back.**Will you stand with me?**[**> > STAND WITH ERIC — DONATE TODAY <<**](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=e55da700ba&e=5f9dc01b8c)Even $10, $25, or $50 makes a real difference. It tells me you have my back. It tells the activist groups that just lost in court — and are already lining up the next round of lawsuits and the next round of candidates — that the voters in this district are paying attention, and we are organized.They spent tens of millions of dollars trying to rewrite the map. They lost. They will be back. So will I.Standing firm,

| Five Questions Maura Healey Needs to Answer Political Spin and Dodging Ends in Election Years
Boston, MA -- In an election year, Governor Maura Healey cannot continue to duck reporters or hide behind friendly media outlets. Massachusetts voters deserve straight answers on public safety, taxes, and fiscal priorities. Here are five questions Governor Healey must address:
Q1. Does Governor Healey regret appointing Parole Board members who continue to release violent criminals early, including murderers originally sentenced to life without parole?
Q2. Does Governor Healey support Mayor Wu's budget cuts to veterans and firefighters, while increasing her own salary and adding patronage hires?
Q3. With nearly 24% of Boston office space sitting empty, what taxes will Governor Healey cut to keep and attract businesses to Massachusetts?
Q4. MassINC's recent poll shows Healey with a 54% unfavorable rating among unenrolled (independent) voters. Why does she think this is happening?
Q5. Following multiple shootings in Boston and Cambridge over the past two weeks, will Governor Healey finally hold criminals accountable?
Massachusetts residents deserve real answers on these critical issues affecting families, businesses, and public safety across the Commonwealth.

# [](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?refcode=&t=1&akid=4756%2E898137%2EtbuVJ-)
I had an idea when we launched our campaign last spring: What about a brewery tour?
I wanted to create events that were open to the public and — dare I say — fun? Because let’s face it, a candidate forum or town hall can be intimidating if you aren’t entrenched in politics.
What’s a normal thing to do? Heading out to grab a drink or a bite to eat with your family and friends.
I thought it would be a great way to ease into the campaign — something we would do throughout the first spring and summer last year.
_Then over 200 people showed up at our first stop._ And we’ve made the events a permanent staple of our campaign. In fact, we just had our 20th _McMorrow on Tap_ stop at Starters in Southfield.
20 stops in, and the message is clear: when we get together, grab a drink, and lower the heat, we can actually talk to each other.
Couldn’t our country use a little more of that these days?
[**So, will you donate $10 or more to my campaign today? Every dollar helps me meet Michiganders across all 83 counties, from union halls to churches, or over a good beer at one of our incredible breweries. 🍺 **](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-may2026._5OkES&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260520_AM1_V1_S1&amount=10&t=2&akid=4756%2E898137%2EtbuVJ-)

I thought it would be a great way to ease into the campaign — something we would do throughout the first spring and summer last year. Then over 200 people showed up at our first stop. And we’ve made the events a permanent staple of our campaign. In fact, we just had our 20th McMorrow on Tap stop at Starters in Southfield. 20 stops in, and the message is clear: when we get together, grab a drink, and lower the heat, we can actually talk to each other. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240852%2E444211%2EyZw296)
My name’s Matthew and I’m a volunteer with Powered by People based in Houston.
**I had a really moving encounter with a Texas transplant this last weekend and I wanted to share what happened with you:**
We were trying something new and going to an apartment complex to interact with voters. My findings were that I had much more success talking to people in the parking lots than on their doorstep (maybe I am too intimidating ).
Anyway, I approached an older woman who had just parked and asked her if she had a moment to talk.
If I am being honest, I had some misgivings about her. She seemed put out, but said she could give me a minute. I told her about the raffle for an HEB card that we were doing for anyone who checked their voter registration.
Begrudgingly she admitted that she "should get registered to vote." She had bad eyesight, so I helped read the form to her so she could fill it out.
In the space between those moments, we started to talk.
She told me about how she had moved to Texas to help take care of her brother and sister-in-law who had since passed away.
She told me about how she was from California and that she was devastated by what was happening in the country.
At some point, I introduced myself and she asked me if I knew what my name meant. Having gone to Catholic school for 10 years of my life, I told her that I did, that it meant "gift from God" and laughed about how that can be a lot of pressure to aspire to. She then proceeded to tell me that her son had been named Matthew, but had also passed away about 4 or 5 years ago (he was about my age now, when he passed).
She said that it was the memory of her son and how upset he was about the "Cheeto Bandito" that inspired her to register to vote with me. We spent another 10 minutes or so trading quotes about the value of being stoic in the face of adversity and the importance of community.
At the end she gave me a hug, thanked me for helping her, and told me that this random conversation in a parking lot today with a stranger was a "gift from God." I'm not crying, you're crying 🥹.
**I'm sharing this because I want you to know exactly what your support makes possible.**
I showed up that day because Powered by People gave me the training, the tools, and the community to do this work.
[**Will you help send more volunteers like me out there? A gift of any size — $10, $25, $100 — goes directly toward reaching voters who are ready to be found.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260520-1.rNIN9d&refcode=ema20260520-240852&t=3&akid=240852%2E444211%2EyZw296)

Thank you,
Matthew

body:
The primary is behind us. Now, we have to win the fight ahead.
[](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260520_1_ak.gv93Je&amount=5&refcode=em20260520-151&t=1&akid=152%2E127862%2Ebd0foX)
It’s Governor Josh Shapiro.
I’m a dad, a husband, the son of a pediatrician and a teacher. **Now, I’m the official Democratic nominee in my reelection campaign for the Governor of Pennsylvania.**
Growing up, my parents taught me about the responsibility to help others and repair the world around us.
Those lessons have guided me my whole life — as a State Rep, County Commissioner, as Attorney General, and now as Governor.
When I-95 collapsed in Pennsylvania, we rebuilt it in 12 days. When families needed relief, we cut taxes. When kids needed a fair shot, we invested in public schools and delivered free breakfast.
And when Donald Trump and the far-right threatened our freedoms, I stood up and fought back.
**Now, I’m running for reelection because all of that progress is on the line.**
But Pennsylvania is one of the toughest battleground states in the country. Trump won here in 2024, and National Republicans think they can win here again. I know we can stop them, but I’ll need every bit of support I can muster.
**[So I’m humbly asking: Will you chip in a donation of any amount — split evenly between our campaign and Aaron Ford — to help us reach our first $25,000 fundraising goal of the general election, win this race on November 3rd, and keep Pennsylvania moving forward?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260520_1_ak.gv93Je&amount=5&refcode=em20260520-151&t=2&akid=152%2E127862%2Ebd0foX)**

Josh

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: Help Free Two Innocent Officers Before It's Too Late
body:
Patriot,
This is a disgrace...and every American who believes in law and order should be furious.
Two police officers—Josh Taylor and Brandon Dingman—are currently serving prison sentences for doing exactly what they were trained and ordered to do: respond to a dangerous call, use non-lethal force, and protecting their community.
Let me tell you what really happened, because the media and the District Attorney certainly won't.
On the night of July 4th, 2019, Officer Josh Taylor responded to a domestic disturbance call in Wilson, Oklahoma. When he arrived, he encountered Jared Lakey: a large, fully grown man walking naked down the street wearing nothing but socks.
Josh immediately recognized this situation for what it was: dangerous and unpredictable. Whether it was drugs, mental illness, or something else—this wasn't a man in his right mind. And Josh knew he couldn't handle it alone. He called for backup.
[Donate to Their Defense](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=41ceb85c2d2145f1a307b7883e6b5b11&_e=Bmp4BUDP_Zln-AD4em1nnHtqJFcu4k5FA86KWU9ufDto9IvW4ygIyWedwn1gD0MnMFjq1h8D4J_OaH2_XIvacxMpTaZYD3Yj_ftehhdriAdkjryOFdHwAC6j-pmrIVQF5pgFbjm7fexqIklNe7E_k7hvDpqmPAdwWX0xdh9KBOYTv2CvHrSQrBt9doZ2absYBzIyO-rTkGYvoNbuN-t63IzsxpdG7WZ9QXCBXPDi65rXNx3BiuDbxhDCVR4Rwd9Wl-ms7ijqfgoR_fULOpvmthquYbhNHBNpdNBz68KR3QDr1oFpa3CWjgiJFYh9soor9fNq1eYeXWwx8XuWGud0UnDcGEjXQmRNj-o_egUVUsVnbpP53pc7_ctGs2PXnKv4C27BiVAlFdHZ6VG29Z9OgimPo-SyVI2HNLe9v-z2-BKPYFjcn60kC_K4lH730s_E)
Officer Josh Taylor
Officer Brandon Dingman
Officer Brandon Dingman arrived on scene, and the two officers tried to do what they were trained to do: safely and professionally bring Mr. Lakey into custody.
But Lakey was 350 pounds, combative, and resisting arrest. When verbal commands didn't work and physical restraint proved impossible, they turned to their department-issued, non-lethal tasers.
They deployed them multiple times, but Lakey kept tearing the barbs out. He was clearly not being fully affected by the tasers—and even after repeated attempts, the officers were unable to subdue him.
Eventually, Josh and Brandon were able to get his arms and cuffed him. They immediately called for medical assistance. An ambulance arrived. Lakey was taken to the hospital.
At that point, the officers had done everything they could—and everything right.
But tragically, Jared Lakey passed away two days later. The autopsy was inconclusive. He had an enlarged heart and lung issues. Drug screenings were unreliable due to the fluids pumped into his system at the hospital. There was no determined cause of death.

| Seven Categories Where Massachusetts Ranks in the Bottom 10 (Worst) Nationally
Dramatic Decline Since 2019: Massachusetts Falls Sharply in Economic Competitiveness
---
---
| Boston, MA -- New analysis by the Massachusetts Republican Party reveals a troubling downturn in the Commonwealth's economic standing since 2019.
Once a national leader, Massachusetts has suffered steep declines in several key competitiveness categories:
* Tax Competitiveness has fallen from 30th-36th nationally to 43rd (bottom 8) in the 2026 Tax Foundation Index, with property taxes now ranked a dismal 48th.
* Cost of Doing Business has plummeted from a strong 14th place in 2019 to 49th (second-worst in the nation) in CNBC's 2025 rankings.
* Electricity Rates remain among the top 3 highest in the country, but now nearly double the national average, with the gap widening.
* Business Formation and Establishment Growth has collapsed from near the top of the nation to the 9th-lowest in total establishment growth.

"These numbers make it clear that the state is rapidly headed in the wrong direction," said Massachusetts Republican Party Chair Amy Carnevale. "High taxes, soaring energy costs, and burdensome regulations are crushing businesses and families."
"It is time to bring back two-party government in Massachusetts for the sake of our future," she concluded.
###.
References
### 1\. Tax Competitiveness
* Rank: 43rd overall (bottom 8) on the 2026 State Tax Competitiveness Index.
* Particularly poor in property taxes (48th) and individual income taxes (42nd). Source: Tax Foundation, 2026 State Tax Competitiveness Index (released late 2025). **Trump Strike Force Responds:** Administration's Scam Center Strike Force led by Jeanine Pirro seized over $700 million in cryptocurrency and issued indictments, as Congress considers the bipartisan Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act.

# NYC Mayor Mamdani meets Dimon amid "Tax The Rich" backlash
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani met with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon and Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon as he intensifies Wall Street outreach **[following backlash over proposals to raise taxes on wealthy residents.](https://substack.com/redirect/f178370d-c15d-414e-9bac-7638141123a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
**Wall Street Outreach Intensifies:** Mamdani held a constructive and friendly first in-person meeting with Jamie Dimon at JPMorgan's new Manhattan headquarters discussing government waste and red tape reduction.

**Additional Key Meetings Held:** Later at Gracie Mansion, Mamdani discussed affordable housing, small-business investment, and retaining talent with Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon.

**Karpathy Joins Pretraining Team:** He starts this week and will build a team using Claude to accelerate pretraining research that helps models acquire core knowledge and capabilities.

# Coca-Cola shuts California plant after a century
Reyes Coca-Cola Bottling will **[permanently close its Ventura Distribution Center in Southern California](https://substack.com/redirect/92dcb774-2e44-4690-b6f7-a12be1efa80d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** this summer after more than a century, impacting 85 employees as the company consolidates operations.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/92dcb774-2e44-4690-b6f7-a12be1efa80d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Ventura Plant Closing:** A large Coca-Cola bottling plant in Southern California will shut down permanently this summer, ending a longstanding relationship between the company and the city.
**WARN Notice Issued:** Reyes Coca-Cola Bottling made the announcement in a May 8 WARN notice, a legally required 60-day heads-up before a major layoff or office closure.
**Jobs Impacted By July:** The closure will impact 85 employees by July 10, with most reassigned to other Southern California facilities and others able to apply for open roles.
**Operations Transferring Now:** The company stated it regularly assesses locations to drive sustainable growth and innovation, transferring operations to other Southern California facilities.

DemocracyDocket: SCOTUS to Hear GOP Lawsuit That Could Radically Restrict Mail Voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052026_1&amount=25]
Team: Mail-in ballots are under attack. Again.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear arguments in RNC v. Wetzel, a lawsuit challenging Mississippi’s law allowing a five-day grace period for late-arriving ballots mailed by Election Day. In simpler terms, it's a case about whether your vote will count if you mail it on or before Election Day, but your ballot arrives after Election Day.
It's clear why a political party -- in this case, the Republican National Committee (RNC) -- is claiming that states must reject ballots that arrive after Election Day. Doing so would potentially disenfranchise a large number of voters, restricting the number of participants in an election. And the data is clear, over the last several election cycles, Republicans have been outnumbered in the use of mail-in ballots.
The RNC is making a blunt decision that their ability to win elections matters more than your vote. It's a cynical attempt to stay in power by suppressing ballots that are delivered late by the postal service. It's the kind of partisan work that shows they'd rather believe in their own power and control than the principles of democracy, of a country where all our votes should count, regardless of party.
Team: We cannot allow blatant partisanship to overrule our right to vote. Help make every mail-in ballot count in Mississippi and beyond with $35 or whatever you can today to make every voice heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052026_1&amount=35]

Our position is clear: If your ballot was postmarked by Election Day, it should count.
This shouldn't be a partisan question. No political party -- Democrat, Republican, Green, Working Families, Libertarian, Reform, Conservative -- should be against voting. No party in our democracy should want to restrict the fundamental right of our fellow citizens to make their voice heard through voting.
But now we're facing a case where the Supreme Court’s decision could strike down or uphold laws in 16 states (and Washington D.C.) allowing late-arriving ballots postmarked on or before Election Day to be counted if they arrive within a set grace period.
How do we know what is at stake? Data from the 2024 Massachusetts elections shows that their three-day grace period for ballots to arrive after Election Day resulted in a 60% drop in rejected ballots as compared to no grace period. That means thousands of votes still counted, more than 1.5% of the total vote count. In a close election, that 1.5% could easily mean the difference between winning and losing.
Our fundamental right to vote should matter so much more than a partisan desperation to win. Chip in $35 or whatever you can to help us defend the use of mail-in ballots and make every vote count in elections nationwide >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=052026_1&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Critics are warning that this fund could be used to pay Trump supporters who have faced federal investigation, like those federally charged in the January 6th attack on our Capitol. | Friend,
We lost the Georgia Supreme Court election last night. Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin ran with courage against a stacked deck: a GOP-controlled commission that attacked them on Election Day, incumbents backed by Governor Kemp's dark money, and a national right-wing machine that has been building toward this moment for thirty years.
We are grateful for their bravery in taking on this machine and devastated they came up short. But we don't have time to lick our wounds--we need to get back to work. Because MAGA is on the march:

| In the past few days, MAGA defeated Republicans Bill Cassidy and Thomas Massie in their primary elections for daring to stand up to Trump. This follows MAGA's Indiana victories punishing state legislators who refused to go along with the election-rigging gerrymandering scheme.
Trump is historically unpopular. Protests are erupting. Every week brings new corruption so brazen it would have ended any previous presidency. The conditions for a historic Democratic wave exist. But the blue wave in November is not inevitable. We have to make it happen.
What happened last night in Georgia is proof. A stacked court, a stacked commission, a governor calling special redistricting sessions, Leonard Leo's dark money flooding the final stretch -- all of it worked together to hold the line for MAGA regardless of the will of voters.
Trump doesn't need to be popular. He just needs to control the courts. And right now, he does. This is exactly why the work of Defend our Courts is critical.
The Georgia loss is a major setback. But it will not stop us. We are 2-1. We have beaten Leo's machine before. We will beat it again -- in the November Supreme Court elections, in the 2026 midterms, and in the fight to reform the Supreme Court via our Unpack our Courts initiative. But only if we double down right now. Not next week. Today.
We cannot afford to lose another state supreme court race.
[Can we count on you to rush a donation of $50, $25, or whatever you can spare -- right now, the morning after our first loss -- to make sure Georgia is the last state supreme court election win that MAGA gets?](https://zzejj9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001SufE-82TCYdNCk3Liz9KjD8hyS6GpvfcmnQpWYkBr5xy1gqc7Ese3RyYgVhZP50ea0nERomR8KhZYCwi1lzYmR7gl8mzEmBG1B1I2UJE9rP2DL9lSnUGUpC1lAtrEjt37tXD2JEsJL_0El4x47cTUELFpaEU6ds84QFuxxBCF93mc2CeX2S3P__58voNM4P7aHRjk-LYhkRYssH5vikEX2G8w8h3jtaO8dNocvLKdRbOX-LVik_0_fuw8PfJduIlcMZ_7vi3WQU=&c=652kMZ0ezYATjXbMyXDGKSsi8rqj8iHJYb0XtEhWVpt4WXyhfHWfwQ==&ch=SFOZY-nTiwpKaBqPvG4yEHfjrfFmizsqg47bgrDvoUXig4gbFN8nwQ==)

Before I ever stepped foot in Washington, I spent more than two decades as a meteorologist here in Illinois. My job was simple: tell people the truth, help them prepare, and look out for them when storms were coming. That experience shaped me more than any political training ever could. In the article, I joked that when I got to Congress, I didn’t just arrive without political baggage, “I didn’t even have political carry-on.” But there’s truth in that. I came here focused on the same things I cared about back then: keeping families safe lowering costs solving problems before they become disasters and earning people’s trust every single day Because trust matters. When severe weather was heading toward the Quad Cities or Rockford, people invited me into their homes. They trusted me in moments when things felt uncertain. I am hosting a **private lunch** for **Pastors & Ministry Leaders** in CD-1 on Tuesday, May 26 at noon at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14795.1.6c4b2f973908070044eec3b996b82a87) in Tulsa about my run for Congress.

Please RSVP to **jackson@jacksonlahmeyer.com** so that we have enough food for everyone.
Also, I am excited to share with you **3 NEW endorsements** that have been released today (more to be announced). 1\. [City Elders](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14796.1.7fe43f52d7bacff1fc93475c4001cb62)

---|---
The race for **OK CD-1** is now _less than 30 days_ away.
I have an urgent need to finish the job to win on Tuesday, June 16.
We have to let every Republican voter know **who I am** and **what I will do** if I am fortunate enough to go to DC on behalf of OK CD-1.
That is going to be done primarily through TV and radio.
Watch the TV AD here: [https://x.com/JacksonLahmeyer/status/2052575682199175406?s=20](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14802.1.2b2840ffeaa4ddb1e9279d3a5082727d)

[**-1 individuals to give $3500**](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14803.1.d36d339981db025cf3838c580132400f)
[**-1 individuals to give $1000**](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14804.1.c8cadc11d4c730194994289aba5b4b2e)

[**-11 individuals to give $25**](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14806.1.75aa8c0bc39ba2a560fee010e2d00b7f)
Will you please consider being one of the **16 individuals** that we need to help us reach our fundraising goal so we can reach the voters of this district?
If you will help us do that it would mean the world to me and I promise to do my best to make you proud.
You can donate here: [https://secure.winred.com/lahmeyer-for-congress/donate-today](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=29994747.14807.1.1d134720f5ac45b9a6fb761615ae1a21)
You can also make checks out to **Lahmeyer For Congress** and mail to:
P.O. Box 470064
9023 E 46th St
Tulsa, OK 74145
I am running for Congress in Oklahoma's 1st District to do several things:
**-Keep Our Borders Secure**
**-Remove Illegal Criminals From Our Streets**
**-Help Make Living In America Affordable For Americans**
**-Not Allowing The Chinese Communist Party To Own American Farmland**
**-Ensuring That Sharia Law Never Takes Root In Our Nation**

Jackson Lahmeyer

**President Donald J. Trump** endorsed me to be the next congressman for OK's 1st district.
**President Trump** called me and said he was endorsing me because he knows I will be a fighter for **Oklahoma Values** and **America First Policies** in Congress.
**President Trump** understands what’s at stake in this moment and that's why he's endorsing me to win this critical seat and join the fight in Congress for the soul of America.
Also, I am excited to share with you that the **ENTIRE Republican House Leadership** has endorsed me for Congress! This includes **Speaker Mike Johnson** , **Leader Steve Scalise** , **Whip Tom Emmer** and **Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain**.
This is **UNHEARD** of support in a crowded Republican Primary.
I would love to earn your support as well!

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635.
